  • 2 tablespoons white vinegar
  • 1 tablespoon sugar
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
  • Fresh dill (optional), chopped for garnish

👩‍🍳 Instructions

  1. Start by thinly slicing the cucumbers using a sharp knife or mandoline. The thin slices allow the cucumbers to absorb the dressing better and keep the salad crisp. Be sure to slice evenly so the salad has a nice texture throughout. Avoid thick slices as they won’t soak up the flavors as well and can feel watery. If your cucumbers have thick skins or lots of seeds, you can peel or deseed them for a smoother texture.
  2. Next, thinly slice the red onion. Thin slices prevent the onion’s sharpness from overpowering the salad. If you want a milder onion flavor, soak the slices in cold water for 5 minutes, then drain before adding to the salad. This step reduces pungency but keeps the crunch. Combine the cucumber and onion slices in a large mixing bowl for even distribution.
  3. In a separate bowl, whisk together the sour cream, white vinegar, sugar, salt, and black pepper until smooth. The vinegar adds a bright tang that balances the creamy sour cream, while the sugar cuts through acidity for a well-rounded flavor. Make sure the sugar dissolves completely to avoid graininess in the dressing.
  4. Pour the dressing over the cucumber and onion slices. Gently toss everything together to coat all the pieces evenly. Be careful not to mash the cucumbers—use a light hand to keep their texture intact. Proper coating ensures every bite is flavorful without being soggy.
  5. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate the salad for at least 30 minutes before serving. This resting time allows the cucumbers and onions to soak up the dressing, mellowing the onions’ bite and blending the flavors beautifully. Skipping this step results in a less flavorful and less cohesive salad.
  6. Before serving, give the salad a gentle stir to redistribute any dressing that may have settled. Taste and adjust seasoning with a pinch more salt or pepper if needed. If desired, sprinkle fresh chopped dill on top for a bright herbal note that complements the creamy tanginess.
  7. Serve the salad chilled as a side dish alongside grilled meats, sandwiches, or as part of a potluck spread. It’s especially refreshing on warm days and pairs well with smoky or spicy flavors. Leftovers keep well and taste even better the next day.
  8. If you want to prepare ahead, slice and dress the cucumbers and onions but wait to add fresh herbs until just before serving to keep their flavor bright. You can also adjust the dressing thickness by adding a splash of milk or water if it thickens too much after chilling.
  9. For a lighter version, substitute Greek yogurt for sour cream. This gives the salad a tangy, protein-rich boost without losing creaminess. Just whisk the yogurt with vinegar and sugar the same way. The flavor will be slightly different but equally delicious.

  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/4 teaspoon black pepper

👩‍🍳 Instructions

  1. Start by slicing your zucchinis into even 1/4-inch thick rounds. Consistent thickness ensures they cook evenly and get tender without turning mushy. If the slices are too thick, they won’t cook through properly; too thin and they might burn or dry out. After slicing, pat them dry with a paper towel to remove excess moisture. This step is crucial because wet zucchini won’t crisp up well in the air fryer and the cheese coating won’t stick properly.
  2. In a bowl, combine the grated Parmesan, shredded mozzarella, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Toss the zucchini slices lightly with olive oil to help the cheese mixture adhere. Then press each zucchini slice firmly into the cheese mixture to coat both sides well. This pressing helps the cheese stick and forms the crispy crust once air fried. Skipping this or not pressing enough can cause the cheese to fall off during cooking.
  3. Preheat your air fryer to 400°F (200°C) for about 3-5 minutes. Preheating is important because it starts cooking the zucchini immediately, helping develop a crispy exterior. If you skip preheating, the zucchini might cook unevenly and become soggy instead of crisp.
  4. Arrange the coated zucchini slices in a single layer in the air fryer basket. Avoid overcrowding to allow hot air to circulate freely, which ensures even cooking and crisping. If you layer them, the zucchini will steam instead of crisp, and the cheese won’t brown properly.
  5. Cook the zucchini at 400°F for 12-15 minutes, flipping halfway through. Flipping is key to get both sides evenly golden and crispy. Watch closely in the last few minutes to avoid burning the cheese. The zucchini should become tender but still hold its shape, with a bubbly, golden crust.
  6. Remove the zucchini from the air fryer and let them cool for a couple of minutes. This resting time helps the cheese crust set and become crispier. Serving immediately can cause the cheese to be too soft and less enjoyable to eat.
  7. Serve your cheesy air fryer zucchini with a dipping sauce like marinara, ranch, or a simple squeeze of lemon. The acidity of lemon brightens the rich cheese and balances the flavors. This step really elevates the dish from simple snack to something special.
  8. If making a larger batch, keep cooked zucchini warm in a low oven (around 200°F) on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. This prevents sogginess and keeps the crust crispy until serving. Avoid stacking slices as that traps steam and ruins texture.
  9. Clean your air fryer basket promptly after use to remove cheese residue and prevent sticking next time. A quick wipe with a damp cloth once cooled is usually enough. Regular cleaning keeps your air fryer performing well and preserves the crispy finish on future batches.

  4. Add the eggs one at a time to the creamed butter and sugar, mixing well after each addition. Then stir in the vanilla extract. Adding eggs gradually helps maintain the emulsion and ensures a smooth batter. If you add them all at once, the batter might curdle or separate.

Let the loaves cool in the pans for 10 minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely.

  • 2 cloves garlic, smashed

  1. Start by washing the banana peppers thoroughly and slicing them into thin rings. The thin slices allow the brine to soak in faster, ensuring every bite is tangy and flavorful.   2. In a medium saucepan, combine the white vinegar, water, sugar, salt, mustard seeds, peppercorns, smashed garlic, and bay leaf. Heat the mixture over medium heat, stirring occasionally until the sugar and salt dissolve completely. This step is crucial as it ensures the brine is balanced and the spices infuse properly. Avoid boiling vigorously, as that can dull the sharpness of the vinegar.
  3. Place the sliced banana peppers into a clean, heatproof jar or container. Pour the hot brine over the peppers, making sure they’re fully submerged. The hot brine helps soften the peppers slightly while preserving their crunch. If peppers float, press them down gently with a spoon or a small weight to ensure even pickling.
  4. Let the jar cool to room temperature before sealing with a lid. Cooling prevents condensation inside the jar, which can dilute the brine and affect shelf life. Once cooled, refrigerate the pickled peppers for at least 24 hours to let the flavors meld. The longer they sit, the more flavorful and tender they become.
  5. After 24 hours, taste a pepper ring to check the flavor. If it’s not tangy enough, let it pickle for another day or two. The vinegar will penetrate deeper over time, mellowing any raw sharpness and bringing out the spices. These pickles are best enjoyed within 2-3 weeks for optimal freshness.
  6. Use the pickled banana peppers as a topping for sandwiches, burgers, or salads. They also make a great side for grilled meats or charcuterie boards. The tangy crunch adds a fresh contrast that livens up any bite. Don’t hesitate to experiment by chopping them into sauces or mixing into dips for added zest.
  7. If you want to store the peppers longer, sterilize canning jars and lids by boiling them for 10 minutes. Pour the hot brine and peppers into the jars, seal tightly, and process in a boiling water bath for 10 minutes. This preserves them safely for several months. Remember to check seals before storing and refrigerate after opening.
  8. For a spicier version, add sliced jalapeños or a pinch of red pepper flakes to the brine. This gives the pickles a nice kick without overwhelming the banana peppers’ bright flavor. Adjust the amount based on your heat preference, adding gradually to avoid overpowering.
  9. Always use clean utensils when removing pickled peppers from the jar to avoid contamination and extend shelf life. Using tongs or a fork prevents introducing bacteria that can spoil your pickles sooner. Keep the jar tightly sealed between uses to maintain crispness and flavor.
